I see the issue! In `_eval_col_insert`, the `entry` function logic has a bug. Let me trace through what happens:

- We have a matrix `self` with shape (rows, cols)
- We're inserting `other` (with shape (other.rows, other.cols)) at position `pos`
- The new matrix should have shape (rows, cols + other.cols)
- For a given (i, j) in the new matrix:
  - If j < pos: we want self[i, j] (columns before the insertion point)
  - If pos <= j < pos + other.cols: we want other[i, j - pos] (the inserted columns)
  - If j >= pos + other.cols: we want self[i, j - other.cols] (columns after the insertion point)

But the current code says:
```python
if pos-3 < j < pos-1:
```
